reviewer: Pickle: official-source down jacket laundry comparison
method: Reviewed the full draft against official sources. Korea Consumer Agency long-padding test of 10 products (Happy Dream, 2019-12-11): all products passed warmth, down-quality, and safety checks, product weight spread 1,066-1,600 g (over 500 g), and the agency advises water washing even for dry-clean-or-wash items because it loses less of the feather's natural oil (유지분), plus tapping clumped down apart, drying fully in the shade, and storing uncompressed. KCA down-parka price-quality briefing on Korea.kr (2014-01-27): lower-limit warmth temperature differed by at most 2.3 C while prices spread 1.4x, KS recommended fillpower/loft (충전도) 120 mm with two brands measured at 111 mm (9 mm short), and fill power marked on raw down can differ from the finished garment so finished-garment markings are preferred. Current care-label standard KS K 0021:2024 (KATS e-National Standards, last confirmed 2024-12-31): symbol temperatures are maximum temperatures (revised from the old 'standard temperature' wording on 2024-03-07), machine-drying symbols split into max 80 C (609) and max 60 C (610), and 30 C delicate/neutral-detergent combinations (113, 117) exist. KCA laundry column (2007-10-29): separate neutral vs mildly-alkaline detergents, dissolve detergent first, pre-soak under 10 minutes, spin about 1 minute. The dry-cleaning vs neutral-detergent experiment (Aekyung commissioned accredited lab, reported by Chosun Biz 2016-02-19 and Segye Ilbo 2016-02-22): after 5 repeated wash cycles with pre-wash values at 100%, fillpower/loft kept 98% (neutral detergent) vs 88% (dry cleaning) and warmth 99.8% vs 87.3%, a 12.5 p gap, attributed to dry-cleaning solvent dissolving the down's natural oils; washing guidance of about 30 C water, neutral detergent, zipped, delicate course, no bleach/fabric softener. Yonsei University graduate thesis (Kim Sunyoung, 2016, published internationally in IJCST 2018): natural fillings (goose/duck down) lose thickness and weight rapidly over 1/2/5/10 wash cycles with sharply declining insulation, and for goose down water washing produced smaller changes than dry cleaning, so water washing suits natural fillings. Herald Economy (2014-11-11): dry-cleaning solvent decomposes feather oil, reducing loft recovery; full wash once per season end or once every two seasons. Laundry-accident compensation: Ministry of Government Legislation EasyLaw (laundry standard terms + FTC consumer dispute standard): compensation = purchase price x rate table, coat average lifespan 4 years, 20x the laundry fee when the receipt was omitted or not issued, claim within 6 months of delivery; FTC notice (KCA PDF): apparel stains/shrinkage resolved 1) free repair 2) exchange 3) refund, and essential detachable parts like a winter-jacket hood are compensated on the whole garment. Waterproofing-spray safety: Korean Journal of Environmental Health Sciences 38(6), 2012 (KCI): a man used about half of a 360 mL fiber waterproofing spray in an unventilated living room, developed vomiting and dyspnea about 2 hours later, was hospitalized with acute interstitial pneumonitis for about 10 days, and two family members also had symptoms; Japan Consumer Affairs Agency column (2024-12-25) lists indoor/vehicle inhalation hospitalization cases and advises masks, outdoor use, wind direction, no spraying near the face, and small amounts. Brand care guidance: Patagonia official product care — down-specific detergent (regular detergent strips natural oils), low-heat tumble dry with 2-3 clean tennis balls (or a large cotton towel) over several cycles, no bleach/ironing/fabric softener, and medium/warm drying renews the DWR finish. All 12 source URLs returned HTTP 200 on 2026-11-02 (the Chosun Biz and Segye pages replaced the bot-blocked News1 link; the ScienceOn thesis record replaced the 403-responding Emerald DOI). Coupang verification: all three ranked products opened in-browser on 2026-11-02 with prices, review counts, and rocket delivery confirmed, and the three freshly issued partner deep links redirect to the correct product IDs with lptag=AF6593875. Plan deviations: the plan's hook claiming 'KCA official test: one dry-cleaning cycle permanently cuts warmth by over 30%' was NOT supported by any official source and was replaced by the verified figures (99.8% vs 87.3% after 5 cycles, manufacturer-commissioned lab, cross-checked with KCA's water-wash recommendation and the Yonsei study); the plan's 'wool dryer balls for fill-power restoration' is grounded in Patagonia's official tennis-ball guidance plus commercially available wool balls; plan item 5's remaining care-label content was grounded in the current KS K 0021:2024 definitions.
